assessment: Five printed pages confirm one binary ptyalism observation in a selected parkinsonism case series. The separately measured autonomic function tests provide no ingredient estimate.
One clinical case describes measured or observed neck-position change after a medication withdrawal. No scored drooling or fig exposure. The case reappears in the Iijima compilation.
The author abstract describes three new medication-associated antecollis cases and a 16-case review. No separate saliva result was reported in the abstract. Preserve case overlap.
One hundred participants provided ten named nonmotor outcomes during on and off states. Dysphagia is measured. The list has no drooling measure.
Table 1 combines two new head-flexion cases and ten prior cases, including Suzuki and two Uzawa cases. No graded saliva outcome or fig exposure.
The outcome comparison concerns four postural angles in 120 Parkinson patients. The proposed link between neck flexion and drooling is discussed without saliva measurement.
The viewpoint and cited SENSE-PARK device study distinguish motor and usability measurements from inclusion of drooling in the symptom background.
The review's dermatitis example reuses the prior Bloem clinical report. The separately discussed sweating findings do not measure saliva loss.
The Swedish registry measured rated saliva loss in 314 people with idiopathic Parkinson disease. The disability index in one analysis includes the drooling item. There is no fig exposure.
